name: Iced Latte

source.name: USDA FoodData Central (FNDDS 2021-2023)

name: Yerba mate (brewed / gourd)

source.name: Caffeine: Bastos DHM, Fornari AC, Queiroz YS, Soares RAM, Torres EAFS (2005) Acta Farm. Bonaerense 24(1):91-95 (HPLC). Macros: USDA FNDDS 'Tea, hot, herbal' (description includes mate tea)
source.description: Tea, hot, herbal (FNDDS; additional descriptions include 'mate tea')
source.crossCheck: FNDDS 2710502 per 100 g: 99.7 g water, 1 kcal, 0.2 g carbs, 1 mg Na, 9 mg K.

notes: Caffeine measured by Bastos et al. on Brazilian brands: one gourd ('cuia', ~500 mL of successive infusions) of chimarrão = 135 mg (27 mg/100 mL); one cuia of cold tereré = 85 mg (17 mg/100 mL); one 182 mL cup of tea-bag mate cocido = 13 mg (7 mg/100 mL). Default is chimarrão; the range covers all three. Real intake depends heavily on leaf load and the number of refills. Macros come from FNDDS herbal tea, whose description explicitly includes mate tea; unlike other herbal teas, mate is caffeinated (Part B's tea_herbal note says not to use it for mate).

source.crossCheck: Martinelli's 8.4 oz single-serve (2596269): 60 kcal, 13.2 g sugar per 100 mL.

notes: Label per 8 fl oz (240 mL): 140 kcal, 31 g sugar (none added), 35 g carbs, 0 mg sodium, 120 mg potassium. 100% carbonated apple juice, nutritionally close to still apple juice (apple_juice). Alcohol-free (alcoholic cider is alc_cider).

name: Clamato (tomato cocktail with clam)

source.name: USDA FoodData Central, Branded Foods (manufacturer label data): Clamato El Original Tomato Cocktail, 8 fl oz (Mott's LLP)
source.crossCheck: Clamato Tomato Cocktail 16 fl oz (2674082): 25 kcal, 4.4 g sugar, 334 mg Na per 100 mL. USDA SR 'Beverages, Clam and tomato juice, canned' (171882): 48 kcal, 3.3 g sugar, 362 mg Na, 87.4 g water per 100 g (older generic).

notes: Label per 8 fl oz: 60 kcal, 10 g sugar (HFCS), 11 g carbs, 800 mg sodium, 170 mg potassium. One of the saltiest drinks in the database (333 mg Na/100 mL, more than tomato juice). Basis of the Canadian Caesar and the Mexican michelada. Contains MSG and dried clam broth.

name: Aloe vera drink

source.name: USDA FoodData Central (SR Legacy)
source.description: Beverages, aloe vera juice drink, fortified with Vitamin C
source.crossCheck: FNDDS 'Aloe vera juice drink' (2709833) reproduces the SR values.

notes: USDA SR per 100 g: 15 kcal, 3.75 g sugar, 8 mg sodium; converted with the record's 240 g per 8 fl oz (1.014 g/mL). Korean-style aloe drinks with pulp (e.g. OKF Aloe Vera King) are usually sweeter, so this is the light end of the category. USDA lists potassium as 0.

name: Agua fresca, tamarind (agua de tamarindo)

source.name: USDA FoodData Central (FNDDS 2021-2023)

notes: FNDDS recipe: 1 qt water + 3/4 lb raw tamarind + 1 cup sugar; per 100 g 109 kcal, 22 g sugar. Converted with FNDDS's 31 g per fl oz (1.048 g/mL). This home recipe is very sweet (~56 g sugar per 240 mL); taquería versions are often diluted further with ice. Other aguas frescas differ: horchata has its own entry, and agua de jamaica is close to sweetened hibiscus tea.

name: Horchata (Mexican rice drink)

source.name: USDA FoodData Central (SR Legacy)
source.description: Beverages, Horchata, as served in restaurant
source.crossCheck: FNDDS 'Horchata, made with water' (2710602): 88 kcal, 8.1 g sugar, 78 g water per 100 g; 'made with milk' (2710603): 91 kcal, 9.6 g sugar.

notes: USDA SR restaurant horchata (water analysed in 3 samples): per 100 g 54 kcal, 9.4 g sugar, 87.1 g water. Converted with the FNDDS horchata portion weight (248 g per cup = 1.048 g/mL) because the SR record's only portion (228 g per cup) looks like it includes ice. The FNDDS recipe-based versions are thicker (78 g water, ~90 kcal/100 g); restaurant horchata is closer to the SR value. Spanish horchata de chufa (tiger nut) is a different drink. Listed as a Part B v2 gap.

name: Oat Milk, barista edition

source.name: USDA FoodData Central, Branded Foods (manufacturer label data): Oatly Barista Edition Oatmilk (Oatly, Inc.)
source.crossCheck: Califia Farms Barista Blend Oatmilk (2509382): 54 kcal, 2.9 g fat, 1.7 g sugar per 100 mL; Elmhurst Barista Edition Oat (2675545): 38 kcal, 0.4 g fat.

notes: Label per 1 cup (240 mL): 140 kcal, 7 g fat (rapeseed oil), 16 g carbs, 7 g sugars (formed when oat starch is broken down enzymatically; labelled as added sugar), 3 g protein, 101 mg sodium, 389 mg potassium. Higher in fat than Oatly Original (plant_oat_original) so it foams; mostly used as a splash or in lattes.

name: Sake (Japanese rice wine)

source.name: Japan Standard Tables of Food Composition (8th rev., 2023 suppl.), MEXT: food 16001, sake, regular (futsushu)
source.crossCheck: USDA SR 'Alcoholic beverage, rice (sake)' (167723) gives 16.1 g alcohol and 134 kcal per 100 g, implying ~20% ABV, which is atypical (flagged in Part B); not used.

notes: MEXT per 100 g: 82.4 g water, 107 kcal, 0.4 g protein, 4.9 g carbohydrate (2.5 g available carbohydrate as monosaccharides), 2 mg Na, 5 mg K, 12.3 g ethanol. Converted with USDA's sake density (29.1 g per fl oz = 0.984 g/mL): 12.1 g ethanol/100 mL = 15.3% ABV, matching typical 15-16% labels. A 180 mL go (the traditional serving) = 21.8 g ethanol = 1.6 US standard drinks. Sugar is not reported separately (null). Premium grades (junmai, ginjo) are similar.

name: Soju (Korean, green bottle)

source.name: Label ABV: Jinro Chamisul Fresh 360 mL, 16% (LCBO product listing)
source.crossCheck: ABV varies by market and year: 15.7-17.8% for 'fresh' green-bottle soju; flavored fruit soju ~12-13%. A UK retailer panel lists 95 kcal/100 mL for a 16.9% Chamisul Fresh.

notes: Only the alcohol is sourced: 16% ABV x 0.789 = 12.6 g ethanol/100 mL, so a 360 mL bottle holds ~45 g ethanol (3.2 US standard drinks) and a 50 mL soju glass ~6.3 g. Ethanol alone supplies ~88 kcal/100 mL; total energy, sugar and water were not found from a primary source, so they are null. Flavored soju (~13%, sweetened) has more sugar and less alcohol.

name: Sangria (red)

source.name: USDA FoodData Central (FNDDS 2021-2023)
source.crossCheck: FNDDS 'Sangria, white' (2710696): 83 kcal, 6.3 g sugar, 7.9 g alcohol per 100 g.

notes: FNDDS recipe: 750 g red table wine + 6 fl oz liqueur + 16 fl oz club soda + lemon juice + 1/8 cup sugar. Per 100 g: 85 kcal, 6.1 g sugar, 8.0 g ethanol (density assumed 1.00, since sugar and ethanol roughly offset) = 10.1% ABV. One FNDDS glass (228 g) = 18 g ethanol = 1.3 US standard drinks. Fruit pieces are not drunk and are not included. Pitcher recipes vary (more juice means less alcohol and more sugar).

name: Mojito

source.name: USDA FoodData Central (FNDDS 2021-2023)

notes: FNDDS recipe: 2 fl oz 80-proof rum + 5.5 fl oz club soda + 16 g lime + 1 tsp sugar + an herb sprig (FNDDS uses cilantro as the herb stand-in for mint). Per 100 g: 61 kcal, 1.8 g sugar, 7.6 g ethanol (density assumed 1.00) = 9.6% ABV. One drink (225 g) = 17 g ethanol = 1.2 US standard drinks. Bar mojitos made with simple syrup are often sweeter.

name: Cosmopolitan

source.name: Composite from USDA: 40 mL 80-proof vodka (SR 174818) + 15 mL orange liqueur (FNDDS 'Liqueur' 2710623, which lists triple sec) + 15 mL lime juice (SR 168156) + 30 mL cranberry juice cocktail (SR 171903)
source.crossCheck: FNDDS 'Martini, flavored' (2710640) names cosmopolitan among its descriptions, but its recipe is 3.5 fl oz spirit with only a teaspoon of cranberry, so it was not used.

notes: Recipe (IBA-style): 40 mL vodka + 15 mL triple sec/Cointreau + 15 mL lime juice + 30 mL cranberry juice cocktail = 100 mL before ice dilution (ignored, as in Part B's composites). Densities: vodka 0.948, liqueur 1.014 (FNDDS 30 g/fl oz), lime 1.041 and cranberry 1.069 (USDA portion weights). Per 100 mL drink: 151 kcal, 9.1 g sugar, 15.9 g ethanol = 1.1 US standard drinks. The generic FNDDS liqueur is ~27% ABV; real Cointreau is 40%, which would add ~1.5 g ethanol per drink.

name: Mimosa

source.name: USDA FoodData Central (FNDDS 2021-2023)

notes: FNDDS recipe: 3 fl oz orange juice + 88 g wine (FNDDS uses white table wine for the sparkling-wine component). Per 100 g: 64 kcal, 4.7 g sugar, 128 mg potassium, 5.0 g ethanol (density 1.00 assumed) = 6.3% ABV. One FNDDS drink (180 g) = 9 g ethanol = 0.6 US standard drinks. A 50/50 flute with Prosecco is similar; more wine raises the alcohol.

name: Aperol Spritz

source.name: Composite: 90 mL Prosecco (USDA FNDDS 'Wine, sparkling' 2710687) + 60 mL Aperol (EU label: 159 kcal, 26.1 g sugar per 100 mL, 11% vol) + 30 mL club soda (USDA SR 174842)
source.crossCheck: The same Aperol per-100 mL panel is reproduced by the Frankfurt Airport shop listing (159.2 kcal, 26.13 g sugar, 0.05 g salt).

notes: Recipe (official 3-2-1): 90 mL Prosecco + 60 mL Aperol + 30 mL soda = 180 mL, ice ignored. Per drink: 163 kcal, 16.6 g sugar (mostly from Aperol), 13.7 g ethanol = 1.0 US standard drinks; ~9.7% ABV in the glass. Water, sodium and potassium are null because Aperol's label gives no water or potassium (its 0.05 g salt/100 mL implies ~20 mg Na but was not used). Prosecco density assumed 0.995.

name: Moscow Mule

source.name: USDA FoodData Central (FNDDS 2021-2023)

notes: FNDDS recipe: 56 g 80-proof vodka (2 fl oz) + 165 g ginger ale + 5 g sugar (USDA has no ginger beer record, so ginger ale plus sugar stands in for the sweeter ginger beer); lime is not included. Per 100 g: 91 kcal, 8.7 g sugar, 8.3 g ethanol (density 1.00 assumed) = 10.5% ABV. One drink (225 g) = 18.7 g ethanol = 1.3 US standard drinks.

name: Bloody Mary

source.name: USDA FoodData Central (FNDDS 2021-2023)

notes: FNDDS recipe: 2 fl oz 80-proof spirit + 5.5 fl oz seasoned tomato juice + Worcestershire, horseradish and chili. Per 100 g: 73 kcal, 2.3 g sugar, 200 mg sodium, 166 mg potassium, 7.8 g ethanol. Density 1.02 assumed (tomato-juice base ~1.03, offset by ethanol) = 10.1% ABV. One drink (225 g) = 17.6 g ethanol = 1.3 US standard drinks and ~450 mg sodium. A Canadian Caesar made with Clamato is saltier still.

name: Mulled wine (glühwein / glögg)

source.name: USDA FoodData Central (FNDDS 2021-2023)

notes: FNDDS recipe: 147 g red table wine + 1 tsp honey + nutmeg; per 100 g 96 kcal, 4.2 g sugar, 10.1 g ethanol (density 1.00 assumed) = 12.8% ABV. Commercial Christmas-market glühwein is often sweeter and weaker (around 7-10% ABV); Nordic glögg with added spirits can be stronger. One 150 mL mug of the FNDDS recipe = 15 g ethanol = 1.1 US standard drinks.

name: Long Island Iced Tea

source.name: USDA FoodData Central (FNDDS 2021-2023)

notes: FNDDS recipe: 2.5 fl oz mixed 80-proof spirits + 1 fl oz sour mix + 124 g cola. Per 100 g: 107 kcal, 8.4 g sugar, 5 mg caffeine (from the cola), 10.4 g ethanol (density 1.00 assumed) = 13.2% ABV. One drink (225 g) = 23 g ethanol = 1.7 US standard drinks; bar versions with five half-ounce spirits are similar or stronger. Listed as a Part B v2 gap.

name: Coffee liqueur (Kahlúa-type)

source.name: USDA FoodData Central (SR Legacy)
source.crossCheck: FNDDS 'Liqueur, coffee flavored' (2710625; Kahlua, Tia Maria) reproduces the SR values.

notes: USDA SR per 100 g: 38.3 g sugar, 46.8 g carbs, 26 mg caffeine, 21.7 g alcohol, 336 kcal; density 1.177 g/mL from USDA's 34.8 g per fl oz. ALCOHOL INCONSISTENCY: 21.7 g/100 g x 1.177 would mean ~32% ABV, but the record is labelled 53 proof (26.5%). alcoholG therefore uses the stated proof (26.5% x 0.789 = 20.9 g/100 mL), and energy = USDA non-alcohol energy (336 - 21.7 x 6.93) x density + 20.9 g x 6.93. Current US Kahlúa and Tia Maria are 20% ABV (~16 g/100 mL), so this overstates alcohol for them. Caffeine ~13 mg per 1.5 fl oz pour.

name: Cream liqueur (Baileys-type)

source.name: USDA FoodData Central (SR Legacy)
source.description: Alcoholic beverage, liqueur, coffee with cream, 34 proof
source.crossCheck: FNDDS 'Liqueur, cream' (2710624; lists Bailey's Irish Cream, RumChata) is a recipe estimate with 33.5 g sugar and 2.7 g fat per 100 g and ~25% ABV, less like Baileys than the SR record.

notes: USDA SR per 100 g: 327 kcal, 19.8 g sugar, 15.7 g fat, 2.8 g protein, 92 mg sodium, 8 mg caffeine, 13.8 g alcohol; density 1.052 from USDA's 31.1 g per fl oz. The computed 14.5 g ethanol/100 mL = 18.4% ABV is slightly above the record's stated 34 proof (17%) and Baileys' 17%, so standard-drink counts are ~8% conservative. A 1.5 fl oz (44 mL) pour = 6.4 g ethanol (0.5 US standard drink) and ~150 kcal.

name: Port / sweet fortified wine

source.name: USDA FoodData Central (SR Legacy)
source.crossCheck: FNDDS 'Wine, dessert, sweet' (2710692; lists sherry, port) reproduces the SR values.

notes: USDA SR per 100 g: 160 kcal, 7.8 g sugar, 13.7 g carbs, 15.3 g alcohol; density 0.9975 from USDA's 29.5 g per fl oz gives 15.3 g ethanol/100 mL = 19.3% ABV (port is typically 19-20%). A 3 fl oz (90 mL) pour = 13.7 g ethanol = 1 US standard drink. Dry fortified wines (fino sherry, dry vermouth): USDA 'wine, dessert, dry' (175112) has less sugar.

name: Hard kombucha (~6% ABV)

source.name: JuneShine Ocean Squeeze product page (manufacturer nutrition panel)
source.crossCheck: Other JuneShine flavors (manufacturer pages, via search): 105-155 kcal, 2-5 g sugar, 6-8 g carbs per 12 oz, all 6% ABV.

notes: Manufacturer panel per 12 fl oz (355 mL): 155 kcal, 8 g carbs, 5 g sugar, 45 mg sodium, 6% ABV (4.7 g ethanol/100 mL; 16.8 g per can = 1.2 US standard drinks). Made on a fermented green-tea base, so some caffeine is likely, but none is declared (null). Water and protein are not on the panel (null). Non-alcoholic kombucha (<0.5%) is other_kombucha.

name: Stout, nitro draught (Guinness-type, 4.2%)

source.name: Guinness Draught published values via secondary sources (Healthline; Food Republic)
source.crossCheck: Food Republic: 125 kcal per 12 oz (https://www.foodrepublic.com/1292700/does-guinness-really-have-as-many-calories-as-bud-light); FatSecret and CalorieKing entries: 126 kcal, 9.4-10 g carbs per 12 oz.

notes: Per 12 fl oz (355 mL): ~125 kcal, ~10 g carbs, ~1 g protein, 4.2% ABV (3.3 g ethanol/100 mL). An imperial pint (568 mL) = 18.8 g ethanol = 2.4 UK units / 1.3 US standard drinks, ~200 kcal. Lower in alcohol and calories than its dark color suggests (less than a regular 5% lager). No primary Diageo panel was read, so values are low confidence; sugar, fat, sodium, potassium and water are null. Foreign Extra Stout (7.5%) is much stronger.
